title: Integrate shared verifier with runner and secure executable resolution
objective: Refactor runner task-completion verification to the shared verification engine while preserving fresh execution of every declared command occurrence and dependency closure, existing allowlist/sandbox enforcement, whole-worktree mutation postconditions, and bounded timeout drainage. Close VC-016 executable-resolution risks in the shared verification core for both direct and runner execution: use one resolver for backend, allowlisted-command, and control-plane Python launches; search only absolute canonical trusted system paths plus toolchain paths declared by the bound profile; reject relative/empty, worktree/control-task-area/sandbox-home/TMPDIR, or group/other-writable search paths; validate toolchain environment selectors; bind resolved canonical executable paths and SHA-256 digests at planning/admission and re-check them at launch; use absolute argv[0] and a trusted child PATH; keep ./gradlew as the explicit worktree-relative code-under-test exception; launch the control-plane interpreter resolved by the shared resolver for every worktree with -I and an explicit environment allowlist that excludes import/startup and loader injection variables.
test_seam: First demonstrate RED for direct and runner execution under hostile executable/import inputs: PATH beginning with dot, relative or worktree directories containing fake python3/git/sandbox-exec/codex; executable bytes changed after qualification; PYTHONPATH, PYTHONHOME, PYTHONSTARTUP, PYTHONUSERBASE, NODE_OPTIONS, LD_PRELOAD, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, DYLD_*, BASH_ENV, ENV, GIT_EXEC_PATH, JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS and sitecustomize injection; JAVA_HOME into the worktree; and a shadow verification package under cwd. Require refusal or trusted absolute executable resolution, no injected marker, and a test proving the shared resolver is the only executable-resolution/launch path. Also prove path canonicalization and writable-ancestor rejection, plan/admission digest binding and launch-time mismatch failure, absolute argv with trusted child PATH, and that the control-plane interpreter is resolved by the shared resolver for every worktree, launched with -I and an explicit environment allowlist. Timeout drainage must be bounded and never treat an unconfirmed drain as terminal or evaluate a false-green postcondition. Preserve existing fresh execution, allowlist, sandbox and whole-worktree mutation regressions. Plan/admission must refuse when executable bindings are absent or mismatched; old plans are replanned, never upgraded in place; swapping executable bytes between planning and launch fails at launch; profile loading refuses an invalid toolchain directory. Case variants of protected control paths (.git, .agent-state and their nested forms) are refused consistently on case-sensitive and case-insensitive filesystems. Backend discovery uses the shared resolver, ignores the inherited PATH, and discovery alone never qualifies a backend; this is tested in T-003's own sandbox tests.
